newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis suggest changes to takeover law.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis suggest changes to takeover law.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that France should consider changing its takeover laws.

"First of all the straightforward information about breaching (stake) thresholds is probably not enough for the market," he told a meeting to inaugurate a financial market watchdog, the Conseil des Marches Financiers.

"I note, from this point of view, that British or American rules which require those buying stakes to declare fairly quickly their intentions as regards the company in which they have bought a stake, are interesting."
He also said that it would be worthwhile exploring an extension of the period for takeover bids, currently limited to 20 trading days.
"I note that the Anglo-Saxon system allows a longer period," he said.
He also suggested considering easing conditions in which a company could intervene to regulate its own shares.

He said, however, that the current rules obliging a bidder to make a takeover offer for all the company's shares once it had crossed a certain treshold were "clear, understandable abroad and very widely accpted".
He als reaffirmed that France planned to introduce pension funds soon but gave no details.
"I must emphasis the introduction soon of retirement savings funds in our country is fundamental for the development of the sharemarket in Paris," he said.
